meta.time_model: virtual wall clock (Comparison\VirtualTime); library code unmodified

libraries.role: Resilience pipeline for PHP HTTP clients: rate limiting, retry with deadline and Retry-After, circuit breaker, bulkhead.
libraries.not_enabled: Only the process-local memory backends were exercised; the Redis backends are a separate package and are not part of this comparison. Real SystemClock/BoundedBlockingScheduler (VirtualClock + VirtualDelayScheduler used, runtime adapter is the real SynchronousRuntimeAdapter). JitterMode::None everywhere (jitter is optional; constant/exponential backoff only). Cooldown policy (shared Retry-After pause) not enabled in any scenario. Fallback operations and FallbackScope not used. EventSink is a NullEventSink except in S18. Pipelines are built through PipelineBuilder + CompiledPipeline (the identity generator is the library default; DeterministicIdentityGenerator is not injected because the public compile() path does not take one and observations contain no identifiers). Every required option with no default (attempt timeout 5 s unless a scenario says otherwise, leases, retry-budget size, probe settings) is chosen per scenario and named in its observation.

libraries.role: Rate limiting (token_bucket, fixed_window, sliding_window policies); admission decision via consume()/reserve().
libraries.not_enabled: Lock factory (not needed for single-process InMemoryStorage), CacheStorage and compound limiters, sliding_window policy (a different algorithm than the scenarios target), reserve()->wait() blocking mode (scenarios use non-blocking consume()).

libraries.role: HTTP client with RetryableHttpClient (retry/backoff/jitter/Retry-After) and ThrottlingHttpClient decorators.
libraries.not_enabled: max_duration / timeout request options (per-request, not enforced by MockHttpClient; see S01), custom RetryStrategyInterface implementations (e.g. one that caps delays), real transports (curl/native), RetryableHttpClient logger (only enabled in S18), multi-base_uri failover.

libraries.role: Guzzle middleware: retry on 429/503 with Retry-After support, optional give_up_after_secs.
libraries.not_enabled: retry_on_methods (default "*" = all methods; restricting it is optional config not enabled in S05 default run), retry_on_timeout, max_allowable_timeout_secs, should_retry_callback, expose_retry_header, on_retry_callback (these are optional; only the options each scenario names were set).

libraries.role: Guzzle middleware that DELAYS (sleeps) requests to stay under N per second/minute (sliding log of timestamps).
libraries.not_enabled: A custom persistent Store (default InMemoryStore is used; cross-process sharing needs a user-written Store), perMinute() limits (scenarios use perSecond).

libraries.role: Circuit breaker (Count and Rate strategies) with pluggable storage; Guzzle middleware and Symfony HttpClient wrapper.
libraries.not_enabled: Redis/Memcached/MongoDB/APCu storage adapters (extensions/servers not present in the image; real Apcu adapter used over an in-process array store), GaneshaHttpClient (Symfony wrapper), custom failure detectors, storage-key customisation, Redis sliding time window (only the tumbling window supported by the Apcu adapter is exercised).

libraries.role: Callable-wrapping pipeline: retry, circuit breaker, timeout (post-hoc deadline), bulkhead, fallback; PSR-14 events; in-memory/PSR-16/Redis state.
libraries.not_enabled: RedisStore / Psr16Store (state backends not in the image; InMemoryStore with the virtual clock is used), PHP attributes / ProxyFactory, fallback(), jitter in Backoff (Backoff::constant used for determinism), event dispatcher (only enabled in S18).

scenarios.title: Total deadline spans retries and waits
scenarios.setup: Total deadline D=10s. Every attempt fails instantly (HTTP 503, no Retry-After). Backoff is a constant 4s. The retry COUNT limit is set high (>=10) so that only a time limit can stop the loop.
scenarios.observed: Start time of every attempt and the time the operation gave up.
scenarios.expected: No attempt starts at or after t=D, and the operation has returned by t=D (attempts at 0,4,8; the wait that would end at 12 is not started).
scenarios.basis: gRPC deadlines are absolute and cover the whole call including retries (grpc.io/docs/guides/deadlines; gRPC A6 retry design: maxAttempts and the call deadline both bind). Google SRE book, Handling Overload.

scenarios.title: Retry-After larger than remaining deadline
scenarios.setup: Deadline D=10s. First response is 503 with Retry-After: 30. Count limit is not binding.
scenarios.observed: Time of any second request and the time the operation returned.
scenarios.expected: A second request is never sent before t=30 (not early) AND the operation returns by t=D (never blocks past the deadline). Together: exactly one request, returned at <= D (as a failure or a deferral).
scenarios.basis: RFC 9110 s10.2.3 (Retry-After: time the client should wait before a follow-up request); deadline semantics as in S01. Surveyed libraries wait uncapped, ignore, or retry early.
scenarios.unsure: RFC 9110 calls the 503 value an "estimate", so "never send before" is a client policy, not a protocol MUST. Retrying early would still be RFC-legal; it is treated as incorrect here because the server asked for a delay.

scenarios.title: Retry-After honoured as a lower bound
scenarios.setup: First response 503 with Retry-After: 6; configured client backoff is a constant 2s. Second sub-case (informational): Retry-After: 1 with configured backoff 4s.
scenarios.observed: Gap between first and second request in each sub-case.
scenarios.expected: Primary: gap >= 6s when the header exceeds the backoff. Informational: with a header smaller than the configured backoff, a lower-bound reading yields gap >= 4s.
scenarios.basis: RFC 9110 s10.2.3; client practice (Dapr wanted the larger of the two; an OpenFGA SDK made the server value override).
scenarios.unsure: Only the primary sub-case decides PASS/FAIL. Whether the header may SHORTEN a configured backoff is contested in practice; the informational sub-case is reported but does not affect the verdict.

scenarios.title: Retry budget bounds retry storms
scenarios.setup: 1000 independent operations all fail with 503. Each operation is allowed up to 3 retries by its own per-operation limit. Delays are zero.
scenarios.observed: Total requests actually sent; extra = total - 1000 first attempts.
scenarios.expected: Aggregate extra traffic is bounded to <= 20% of first attempts (SRE guidance is ~10%; 20% allows burst slack), independent of the per-operation limit. Unbounded per-operation retries give +300%.
scenarios.basis: Google SRE book, Handling Overload (per-client retry budget ~10%; bounds worst case near 1.1x instead of ~3x); AWS Builders Library, Timeouts, retries and backoff with jitter (retry amplification).
scenarios.unsure: The 20% threshold is this harness's choice. A circuit breaker also bounds extra traffic but by stopping primary traffic too; if a library offers both, retry-only and breaker variants are reported separately.

scenarios.title: Non-idempotent POST is not retried by default
scenarios.setup: Default retry configuration (only delays zeroed). A POST receives (a) HTTP 500, (b) a transport failure. Informational: (c) 503, (d) 429.
scenarios.observed: Number of requests sent in each sub-case.
scenarios.expected: Sub-cases (a) and (b): exactly 1 request (the server may have processed it).
scenarios.basis: RFC 9110 s9.2.2 (idempotent methods; automatic retry of others is not safe); AWS Builders Library (retry only idempotent operations or use idempotency keys).
scenarios.unsure: Sub-cases (c)/(d) are informational: 429/503 are often sent before processing and several libraries retry them for any method; the RFC does not declare that safe, but it is common practice. They do not affect the verdict.

scenarios.title: Token bucket exact boundary and refill remainder
scenarios.setup: Capacity (burst) 2, refill 1 token per 2s, bucket starts full at t=0. Take 2 tokens at t=0. Probe at t=1.999 and t=2.0. Then jump to t=5.0 and probe; probe at t=5.999 and t=6.0.
scenarios.observed: Admit/reject decision at each probe instant.
scenarios.expected: t=0 third request rejected. t=1.999 rejected (no early admission). t=2.0 admitted, then rejected again. At t=5.0 exactly one token has accrued (admitted once, then rejected) and the 1.0s remainder toward the next token is preserved: t=5.999 rejected, t=6.0 admitted.
scenarios.basis: Token bucket definition: admissions in any interval of length T never exceed burst + rate*T; a refill remainder must not be discarded (generic definition, e.g. Wikipedia "Token bucket").

scenarios.title: Fixed/sliding window boundary: no early admission
scenarios.setup: Limit 3 requests per window W (W=10s; W=1s where the library only offers a 1s unit). All 3 are admitted at t0. Probe the 4th request just before, at, and just after t0+W.
scenarios.observed: Decision (or the instant a delaying limiter lets it through) at t0+W-0.001, t0+W, t0+W+0.001.
scenarios.expected: The 4th request is not admitted before t0+W and is admitted no later than t0+W+0.001s.
scenarios.basis: Definition of an N-per-window limit: safety (no early admission) and liveness (admission once the window has elapsed).
scenarios.unsure: Whether admission occurs at exactly t0+W or one tick later is an open/closed-interval implementation choice; only "not early" and "within 1ms" are required.

scenarios.title: Circuit opens exactly at threshold and minimum samples
scenarios.setup: Minimum samples 4, failure-rate threshold 50% (count threshold 4 where the library only has that). Seq1: four failures. Seq2: success,success,failure,failure (exactly 50% at the 4th sample). Seq3: success,success,success,failure (25%).
scenarios.observed: After each sequence, whether the next call is admitted; and for Seq1 whether the 4th call was still admitted after 3 failures.
scenarios.expected: Seq1: calls 1-4 execute, call 5 rejected. Seq2: call 5 rejected. Seq3: call 5 admitted.
scenarios.basis: Resilience4j CircuitBreaker docs: opens when the failure rate is equal to or greater than the threshold, only after minimumNumberOfCalls.
scenarios.unsure: Rate semantics differ across libraries (some key counters by time window, count strategies have no rate). Each adapter uses the closest native configuration and states it.

scenarios.title: Half-open admits only the configured probes
scenarios.setup: Circuit open; cooldown elapsed. Five callers arrive before any probe has reported. Probe limit P=2 (P=1 where the library offers no setting).
scenarios.observed: How many of the five callers were allowed to execute.
scenarios.expected: Exactly P execute; the rest are rejected.
scenarios.basis: Resilience4j permittedNumberOfCallsInHalfOpenState; Polly circuit breaker half-open semantics.

scenarios.title: An abandoned probe neither closes the circuit nor wedges it forever
scenarios.setup: Circuit open, cooldown (30s) elapsed, a probe is admitted and never reports (worker died or was cancelled). Other callers arrive immediately, and again after a further 1.5x cooldown.
scenarios.observed: Do callers pass freely after the abandonment? Is a replacement probe admitted later?
scenarios.expected: Not closed right after abandonment (no free passage), and a replacement probe is admitted within 2x cooldown.
scenarios.basis: Safety (an unreported probe is not evidence of recovery) and liveness (probe leases/timeouts); design principle.
scenarios.unsure: No external standard specifies abandoned-probe handling; the expectation is a design principle, not a citable rule.

scenarios.title: A stale result after reopen cannot change breaker state
scenarios.setup: Call A starts while closed (t=0) and is slow. The circuit opens at t=0 (4 failures, cooldown 30s). At t=31 a probe fails and the circuit reopens (next probe due t=61). A completes at t=40: variant (i) with a failure, variant (ii) with a success.
scenarios.observed: (i) Is a probe admitted at t=60.999 / t=61.001? (ii) Is the circuit still open at t=45?
scenarios.expected: (i) next probe still due at t=61 (rejected at 60.999, admitted at 61.001). (ii) circuit remains open at t=45.
scenarios.basis: Late results from a previous circuit generation carry no information about the dependency's current state (generation/fencing guard).
scenarios.unsure: No external standard; Resilience4j/Polly documentation does not address it. Treated as a correctness property the project claims.

scenarios.title: Late/non-owner release cannot free someone else's permit
scenarios.setup: Concurrency limit 1, lease 1s. Holder A exceeds its lease. B is then admitted (lease expired). A finishes (late release) while B still runs. C arrives while B is running.
scenarios.observed: Is C admitted while B is still running?
scenarios.expected: C is rejected; peak concurrency never exceeds 1. A's late release must not release B's permit.
scenarios.basis: Fencing-token / ownership principle for leases (Kleppmann, "How to do distributed locking").

scenarios.title: Cancel before dispatch leaves no leaked capacity
scenarios.setup: A caller is admitted (permit taken) and is cancelled by its own cancellation signal before the transport callback is dispatched. Capacity is then probed with a fresh caller.
scenarios.observed: Is the permit returned?
scenarios.expected: Capacity is fully returned.
scenarios.basis: Resource-safety invariant: every acquired permit has exactly one release on all exits, including cancellation.
scenarios.unsure: Libraries without a cancellation concept are NOT_EXPRESSIBLE, not FAIL.

scenarios.title: Permit released when the callback throws
scenarios.setup: Concurrency limit 1. The callback throws an Exception, then (separately) a PHP Error.
scenarios.observed: After each throw, is a new caller admitted?
scenarios.expected: Yes for both.
scenarios.basis: try/finally resource-safety invariant.

scenarios.title: Rate quota consumed equals requests actually sent
scenarios.setup: One logical GET fails twice with 503 then succeeds (3 wire requests). Retry and rate limiting are composed in both possible orders; quota is large enough never to block. Sub-case: a request cancelled before it is sent.
scenarios.observed: Quota units consumed vs. requests that reached the mock transport, per composition order.
scenarios.expected: consumed == sent for every composition order: retries count against the quota, and quota is not spent on requests never sent.
scenarios.basis: A rate limit protects the downstream so it must count wire traffic including retries (AWS Builders Library, retry amplification).
scenarios.unsure: Many designs deliberately leave composition order to the user. Reported as FAIL with gap "composition-dependent" when one order is correct and the other is not.

scenarios.title: Typed, machine-readable rejection taxonomy
scenarios.setup: Provoke every rejection or give-up cause the library itself produces (rate-limited, circuit-open, bulkhead-full, deadline exceeded, retries exhausted).
scenarios.observed: Per cause: distinguishable by exception class/enum (not message text)? Do rate/circuit rejections carry a machine-readable earliest-retry time or duration?
scenarios.expected: Every produced cause has its own type, and rate-limit and circuit-open rejections expose a retry-at / retry-after value.
scenarios.basis: Engineering practice: callers branch on type, not on message text; Retry-After precedent in RFC 9110.
scenarios.unsure: Judgement-heavy; not a published standard. The "retry-at on circuit-open" clause is the harness author's requirement. Facts (type list, fields) are reported so a reader can re-grade.

scenarios.title: Wall-clock regression safety
scenarios.setup: A time-based limiter/breaker is exhausted at t=T. The wall clock then jumps BACK by 3600s. One full configured interval of elapsed (monotonic) time passes.
scenarios.observed: Does the component admit again after one interval of elapsed time, or stall until the clock catches up? Does it ever over-admit?
scenarios.expected: No over-admission, and recovery within <= 2x the configured interval of elapsed time (stall bounded, not ~3600s).
scenarios.basis: Durations should be measured with a monotonic clock (Linux clock_gettime(2) CLOCK_MONOTONIC is not affected by discontinuous jumps; PHP hrtime()).
scenarios.unsure: State shared across processes needs a shared (wall) clock, so full immunity is impossible there; only a bounded stall is required. A stall is the safe direction (no over-admission) but is an availability loss.

scenarios.title: Throwing observer does not change the business result
scenarios.setup: An event sink / logger / subscriber that throws on every event is attached. The operation (retry once then succeed, or a circuit trip) runs.
scenarios.observed: Is the business result (return value / completion) identical to the run without the observer?
scenarios.expected: Identical result; observer failure is contained.
scenarios.basis: OpenTelemetry specification, "Error handling in OpenTelemetry": instrumentation must not throw into application code.
scenarios.unsure: PSR-14 does not require a dispatcher to swallow listener exceptions, so a library can argue propagation is the dispatcher's job. The expectation reflects the telemetry principle, not PSR-14.

scenarios.title: Runtime dependency count (transitive)
scenarios.setup: Transitive closure of "require" (excluding php, ext-*, lib-*) for the package as resolved in this harness's composer.lock.
scenarios.observed: Count and list of packages.
scenarios.expected: No verdict (measurement). Reqtide Core targets zero runtime dependencies.
scenarios.basis: composer.lock of the harness; equivalent to the packages reachable by "composer why".
scenarios.unsure: The count depends on the resolved set; shared transitive packages are counted per package.

scenarios.title: PHP floor
scenarios.setup: The "php" constraint of the pinned release and the "php" constraints in its dependency closure.
scenarios.observed: Constraint strings from composer metadata.
scenarios.expected: No verdict (measurement).
scenarios.basis: composer.lock of the harness.

scenarios.title: Static analysis preserves the callback return type (generics)
scenarios.setup: PHPStan analyses $r = <library entry point that executes a callback returning int>; dumpType($r).
scenarios.observed: The type PHPStan infers for $r.
scenarios.expected: int (a @template return preserved through the execution API).
scenarios.basis: PHPStan generics via PHPDoc (@template).

reqtide.observation: PHPStan max: $r = $pipeline->execute(fn (AttemptContext $a): int => opaque(), $pipeline->newContext(Duration::seconds(5))) is inferred as "int".
